content.shloka:
Siya Ram Siya Ram Siya Ram,
Jai Jai Ram Jai Jai Ram Jai Siya Ram.
content.meaning: Glory to Sita and Rama! Chanting their sacred names together brings divine grace, for Sita and Rama are inseparable — the eternal union of devotion and the Divine.
content.transliteration:
Sīyā Rām Sīyā Rām Sīyā Rām,
Jai Jai Rām Jai Jai Rām Jai Sīyā Rām.

content.shloka:
Siya Ram Siya Ram kahiye,
Jahi vidhi rakhe Ram tahi vidhi rahiye.
content.meaning: Keep chanting the names of Sita and Rama. However the Lord keeps you, remain content in that state — surrender to His divine will.
content.transliteration:
Sīyā Rām Sīyā Rām kahiye,
Jāhī vidhi rākhe Rām tāhī vidhi rahiye.

content.shloka:
Mangal bhavan amangal hari,
Dravahu so Dasharath Ajir bihari.
content.meaning: He who is the abode of auspiciousness and the destroyer of all inauspiciousness — may that Lord Rama, the delight of King Dasharatha's courtyard, shower His grace upon us.
content.transliteration:
Maṅgal bhavan amaṅgal hārī,
Dravahu so Daśaratha Ajira bihārī.

content.shloka:
Raghupati Raghav Raja Ram,
Patita Pavan Sita Ram.
Sita Ram Sita Ram,
Bhaj pyare tu Sita Ram.
content.meaning: O Lord Rama, chief of the Raghu dynasty! O Redeemer of the fallen, Sita-Rama! Beloved one, chant the sacred names of Sita and Rama.
content.transliteration:
Raghupati Rāghav Rājā Rām,
Patita Pāvan Sītā Rām.
Sītā Rām Sītā Rām,
Bhaj pyāre tū Sītā Rām.

content.shloka:
Ishwar Allah tero naam,
Sab ko sanmati de Bhagavan.
content.meaning: Whether called Ishwar or Allah, it is Your name, O Lord. Bless everyone with right understanding and noble thoughts.
content.transliteration:
Īśvar Allāh tero nām,
Sab ko sanmati de Bhagavān.

content.shloka:
Hare Krishna Hare Krishna,
Krishna Krishna Hare Hare.
Hare Rama Hare Rama,
Rama Rama Hare Hare.
content.meaning: O Supreme Energy (Hare)! O All-Attractive Lord (Krishna)! O Source of All Pleasure (Rama)! Please engage me in Your devotional service. This Mahamantra is the supreme means of deliverance in the age of Kali.
content.transliteration:
Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa,
Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare.
Hare Rāma Hare Rāma,
Rāma Rāma Hare Hare.

content.shloka:
Cheto darpana marjanam bhava maha-davagni nirvapanam,
Shreyah kairava chandrika vitaranam vidya vadhu jivanam.
content.meaning: The chanting of the Holy Name cleanses the mirror of the heart, extinguishes the blazing fire of material existence, spreads the moonlight of auspiciousness, and is the life of all transcendental knowledge.
content.transliteration:
Ceto-darpaṇa-mārjanaṁ bhava-mahā-dāvāgni-nirvāpaṇaṁ,
Śreyaḥ-kairava-candrikā-vitaraṇaṁ vidyā-vadhū-jīvanam.

content.shloka:
Anandambudhi vardhanam prati padam purnamritasvadanam,
Sarvatma snapanam param vijayate Shri Krishna Sankirtanam.
content.meaning: The congregational chanting of Krishna's name increases the ocean of transcendental bliss, enables tasting of full nectar at every step, and bathes the entire self in divine joy. All glories to the Sankirtana of Lord Krishna!
content.transliteration:
Ānandāmbudhi-vardhanaṁ prati-padaṁ pūrṇāmṛtāsvādanaṁ,
Sarvātma-snapanaṁ paraṁ vijayate Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtanam.

content.shloka:
Namnam akari bahudha nija sarva shaktis,
Tatrarpita niyamitah smarane na kalah.
Etadrishi tava kripa bhagavan mamapi,
Durdaivam idrisham ihajani nanuragah.
content.meaning: O Lord, Your Holy Name bestows all benedictions. You have invested all Your transcendental energies in these Names. There are no hard rules for chanting. O Lord, You are so kind — yet my misfortune is that I have no attraction for Your Name.
content.transliteration:
Nāmnām akāri bahudhā nija-sarva-śaktis,
Tatrārpitā niyamitaḥ smaraṇe na kālaḥ.
Etādṛśī tava kṛpā bhagavan mamāpi,
Durdaivam īdṛśam ihājani nānurāgaḥ.

content.shloka:
Harer nama harer nama harer namaiva kevalam,
Kalau nasty eva nasty eva nasty eva gatir anyatha.
content.meaning: In this age of Kali, the Holy Name of the Lord, the Holy Name of the Lord, the Holy Name of the Lord alone is the only way, the only way, the only way — there is no other path.
content.transliteration:
Harer nāma harer nāma harer nāmaiva kevalam,
Kalau nāsty eva nāsty eva nāsty eva gatir anyathā.

content.shloka:
Om Namah Shivaya, Om Namah Shivaya,
Om Namah Shivaya, Om Namah Shivaya.
content.meaning: I bow to Lord Shiva, the auspicious one. This Panchakshari mantra invokes the five elements and the grace of Mahadeva, the supreme consciousness.
content.transliteration:
Oṁ Namaḥ Śivāya, Oṁ Namaḥ Śivāya,
Oṁ Namaḥ Śivāya, Oṁ Namaḥ Śivāya.

content.shloka:
Kar le Shiv ka dhyan, O man ke musafir,
Na jaane kab ho jaaye tera ant safar.
content.meaning: O traveller of the mind, meditate on Lord Shiva. You never know when your final journey will begin — so take refuge in Him now.
content.transliteration:
Kar le Śiv kā dhyān, o man ke musāfir,
Nā jāne kab ho jāye terā ant safar.

content.shloka:
Bam Bam Bhole Bam Bam Bhole,
Devo ke Dev Mahadeva.
Bam Bam Bhole Bam Bam Bhole,
Bhole Nath Mahadeva.
content.meaning: Hail Bholenath, hail the innocent Lord! The God of all gods, Mahadeva! Shiva, who is easily pleased by sincere devotion.
content.transliteration:
Bam Bam Bhole Bam Bam Bhole,
Devo ke Dev Mahādevā.
Bam Bam Bhole Bam Bam Bhole,
Bhole Nāth Mahādevā.

content.shloka:
Shiv Shiv Shiv Shiv Shivaya Namah Om,
Hara Hara Hara Hara Namah Shivaya.
Adi Dev Mahadev Karuna Nidhe,
Ab to dayal daya kijiye.
content.meaning: Salutations to Lord Shiva again and again! O Primordial God, great Lord, treasure of compassion — O merciful one, please bestow Your grace upon us now.
content.transliteration:
Śiv Śiv Śiv Śiv Śivāya Namaḥ Oṁ,
Hara Hara Hara Hara Namaḥ Śivāya.
Ādi Dev Mahādev Karuṇā Nidhe,
Ab to dayāl dayā kījiye.

content.shloka:
Namo Namo Shankara Bholenath,
Tumhi ho jagat ke swami.
Kailashi Nath Parvati Pati,
Meri bigdi bana do Swami.
content.meaning: Salutations again and again to Lord Shankara, the innocent Lord. You alone are the master of the universe. O Lord of Kailash, husband of Parvati, please set right my troubled life.
content.transliteration:
Namo Namo Śaṅkara Bholenāth,
Tumhī ho jagat ke svāmī.
Kailāśī Nāth Pārvatī Pati,
Merī bigaḍī banā do Svāmī.

content.shloka:
Jai Mata Di, Jai Mata Di,
Bolo sada Jai Mata Di.
Jagdamba Jai Jai, Maa Jai Jai,
Bolo sada Jai Mata Di.
content.meaning: Hail to the Divine Mother! Always chant 'Victory to Mother.' Hail to Jagdamba, the Mother of the Universe — always proclaim Her glory.
content.transliteration:
Jai Mātā Dī, Jai Mātā Dī,
Bolo sadā Jai Mātā Dī.
Jagdambā Jai Jai, Mā Jai Jai,
Bolo sadā Jai Mātā Dī.

content.shloka:
Ambe tu hai Jagdambe Kali,
Jai Durge khappar wali.
Tera hi gun gaave Bharati,
O Maiya hum sab utare teri aarti.
content.meaning: O Amba, you are Jagdamba, you are Kali! Victory to Durga, the fierce protector. All of India sings your praises — O Mother, we offer you this sacred aarti.
content.transliteration:
Ambe tū hai Jagdambe Kālī,
Jai Durge khappar vālī.
Terā hī guṇ gāve Bhāratī,
O Maiyā ham sab utāre terī āratī.

content.shloka:
Bigdi meri bana do, Sheronwali Maa,
Apni sharan mein lelo, Maiya Maa.
Teri jai ho Durge, Maata rani,
Sunte sab ki Maiya, Antaryami.
content.meaning: O Mother who rides the lion, set right my troubled life. Take me into Your shelter, O Divine Mother. Victory to You, O Queen Mother Durga — You listen to all, O All-Knowing One.
content.transliteration:
Bigaḍī merī banā do, Śeronvālī Mā,
Apnī śaraṇ meṁ le lo, Maiyā Mā.
Terī jai ho Durge, Mātā Rānī,
Sunte sab kī Maiyā, Antaryāmī.

content.shloka:
Jhulat Radhe rani jhulat maha rani,
Nau Durga ke naam sada sukhdayani.
Shailputri Brahmacharini Chandraghanta Maa,
Kushmanda Skandmata Katyayani Maa.
content.meaning: The great Queen swings in joy. The nine forms of Durga always bestow happiness — Shailputri, Brahmacharini, Chandraghanta, Kushmanda, Skandamata, and Katyayani.
content.transliteration:
Jhūlat Rāḍhe Rānī jhūlat Mahā Rānī,
Nau Durgā ke nām sadā sukhdāyanī.
Śailputrī Brahmacāriṇī Candraghaṇṭā Mā,
Kūṣmāṇḍā Skandamātā Kātyāyanī Mā.

content.shloka:
Vitthala Vitthala Vitthala Hari,
Panduranga Vitthala Hari.
Pundalik varada Hari Vitthala,
Sri Dnyandev Tukaram.
content.meaning: Chant the name of Vitthala, Lord Hari of Pandharpur! He who blessed devotee Pundalik — salutations to Him whose glories were sung by Dnyaneshwar and Tukaram.
content.transliteration:
Viṭṭhala Viṭṭhala Viṭṭhala Hari,
Pāṇḍuraṅga Viṭṭhala Hari.
Puṇḍalīk varadā Hari Viṭṭhala,
Śrī Jñāndev Tukārām.

content.shloka:
Jya sukhaasi karane, dev vedha zhale,
Te sukha sahaje santal ladhale.
Jethe Naama ghoshi Hari Vitthalachi,
Tethe kripa varse Pandurangachi.
content.meaning: The bliss that even the gods long for, the saints have effortlessly attained. Wherever the Name of Hari Vitthala resounds, there the grace of Panduranga showers down.
content.transliteration:
Jyā sukhāsī kāraṇe, dev vedhā jhāle,
Te sukh sahaje santāṁl lādhale.
Jethe Nāma-ghoṣī Hari Viṭṭhalachī,
Tethe kṛpā varse Pāṇḍuraṅgācī.

content.shloka:
He Vitthal bara poriye, sandavali waari.
Changdev watalit, jnyane padari.
Eka janardani, bhav sindhu taari.
content.meaning: O Vitthala, how wonderful! The Wari pilgrimage flourishes. Changdev bowed, Dnyaneshwar placed His feet. Lord Janardana carries us across the ocean of worldly existence.
content.transliteration:
He Viṭṭhal barā poriye, sāṇḍavalī vārī.
Cāṅgdev vāṭalīt, Jñāne paḍarī.
Ekā Janārdanī, bhav-sindhu tārī.

content.shloka:
Mauli Mauli, Dnyanoba Mauli,
Tukaram Mauli re.
Pandharichi vari geli Devachi nagari,
Sangati karuni Dnyanoba Tukaram.
content.meaning: O beloved Mauli (Mother-Guru)! Dnyanoba is our Mauli, Tukaram is our Mauli. The Wari pilgrimage has reached the city of God — in the sacred company of Dnyanoba and Tukaram.
content.transliteration:
Māulī Māulī, Jñānobā Māulī,
Tukārām Māulī re.
Paṇḍharīcī vārī gelī Devācī nagarī,
Saṅgatī karunī Jñānobā Tukārām.

content.shloka:
Yei ho Vitthale, Maaze maahera Pandhari.
Aavad mala bhetalaa Maher Pandhari,
Vithe bhivare ubha, vitevari.
content.meaning: Come, O Vitthala! Pandharpur is my maternal home. I have found the joy of my mother's home in Pandhari. On the banks of the river Bhima, He stands upon the brick.
content.transliteration:
Yeī ho Viṭṭhale, māze māhera Paṇḍharī.
Āvaḍ malā bheṭalā Māher Paṇḍharī,
Viṭhe bhīvare ubhā, viṭevarī.

content.shloka:
Bajrang Baan padhe Hanuman,
Sankat kate Mahavir Hanuman.
Jai Hanuman, Jai Jai Hanuman,
Pavan putra bali Hanuman.
content.meaning: Hanuman, who recites the Bajrang Baan, destroys all calamities. Victory to Hanuman, the mighty son of the Wind God! Hail to the most powerful Hanuman.
content.transliteration:
Bajraṅg Bāṇ paḍhe Hanumān,
Saṅkaṭ kaṭe Mahāvīr Hanumān.
Jai Hanumān, Jai Jai Hanumān,
Pavan putra balī Hanumān.

content.shloka:
Ram lakhana sita man basiya,
Shri Hanuman ji ke hriday basiya.
Sabke sankat door karo, Mahaveer,
Bhakton ke hriday mein nit nit basiye.
content.meaning: Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita dwell in His heart. Shri Hanuman resides in the hearts of all devotees. O Great Warrior, remove the troubles of all — dwell eternally in the hearts of Your devotees.
content.transliteration:
Rām Lakhan Sītā man basiyā,
Śrī Hanumān jī ke hṛday basiyā.
Sabke saṅkaṭ dūr karo, Mahāvīr,
Bhaktoṁ ke hṛday meṁ nit nit basiye.

content.shloka:
Jai Jai Jai Hanuman Gosaai,
Kripa karahu Gurudev ki naai.
Jo sat baar paath kar koi,
Chutehi bandi maha sukh hoi.
content.meaning: Glory, glory to Lord Hanuman! Bestow grace like a supreme guru. Whoever recites this a hundred times is freed from all bondage and attains great happiness.
content.transliteration:
Jai Jai Jai Hanumān Gosāīṁ,
Kṛpā karahu Gurudev kī nāīṁ.
Jo śat bār pāṭh kar koī,
Chūṭehi bandī mahā sukh hoī.

content.shloka:
Sankat mochan naam tiharo,
Sumirat hiye sankat sab haro.
Ram Lakhan Sita sahit Hanuman,
Hriday basahu sur bhup Bhagwan.
content.meaning: Your name is the Reliever of Afflictions. Remembering You in the heart, all troubles vanish. May Rama, Lakshmana, Sita along with Hanuman forever dwell in our hearts, O Supreme Lord.
content.transliteration:
Saṅkaṭ Mocan nām tihāro,
Sumirat hiye saṅkaṭ sab hāro.
Rām Lakhan Sītā sahit Hanumān,
Hṛday basahu sur bhūp Bhagavān.

content.shloka:
Jai Ganesh Jai Ganesh Jai Ganesh Deva,
Mata jaki Parvati Pita Mahadeva.
content.meaning: Victory to Lord Ganesh! His mother is Goddess Parvati and His father is Lord Mahadeva (Shiva). He is worshipped first among all deities.
content.transliteration:
Jai Gaṇeś Jai Gaṇeś Jai Gaṇeś Devā,
Mātā jākī Pārvatī Pitā Mahādevā.

content.shloka:
Ek dant dayavant char bhuja dhari,
Maathe par tilak sohe muse ki savari.
Andhon ko aankh det kodhiyon ko kaaya,
Baanjhan ko putra det nirdhan ko maya.
content.meaning: Single-tusked, compassionate, four-armed Lord, a sacred mark adorns His forehead, riding a mouse. He gives sight to the blind, heals the lepers, blesses the childless with sons, and grants wealth to the poor.
content.transliteration:
Ek dant dayāvant cār bhujā dhārī,
Māthe par tilak sohe mūse kī savārī.
Andhon ko āṅkh det koḍhiyon ko kāyā,
Bāṅjhan ko putra det nirdhan ko māyā.

content.shloka:
Haar chadhe phool chadhe aur chadhe meva,
Ladduan ka bhog lage sant kare seva.
content.meaning: Garlands are offered, flowers are offered, dry fruits are offered. He is pleased with offerings of laddu sweets, and the saints serve Him with devotion.
content.transliteration:
Hār caḍhe phūl caḍhe aur caḍhe mevā,
Laḍḍuaṁ kā bhog lāge sant kare sevā.

content.shloka:
Deenan ki laaj rakho Shambhu sutkaari,
Kamna ko puri karo Jai Girijaa ke dulhaari.
Jai Ganesh Jai Ganesh Jai Ganesh Deva,
Mata jaki Parvati Pita Mahadeva.
content.meaning: Protect the honour of the humble, O Son of Shambhu. Fulfil our wishes, O beloved of Mother Girija. Victory to Lord Ganesh, whose mother is Parvati and father is Mahadeva!
content.transliteration:
Dīnan kī lāj rākho Śambhu sutkārī,
Kāmnā ko pūrī karo Jai Girijā ke dulhārī.
Jai Gaṇeś Jai Gaṇeś Jai Gaṇeś Devā,
Mātā jākī Pārvatī Pitā Mahādevā.

content.shloka:
Payoji maine Ram Ratan Dhan payo,
Vastu amolak di mere Satguru,
Kirpa kar apnayo.
content.meaning: I have found the priceless jewel of the Lord's name! My true Guru graciously bestowed upon me this invaluable treasure and accepted me as His own.
content.transliteration:
Pāyojī maine Rām Ratan Dhan pāyo,
Vastu amolak dī mere Satguru,
Kṛpā kar apnāyo.

content.shloka:
Janam janam ki punji paai,
Jag mein sabhi khovayo.
Khevanh nahin koi takkar laagat,
Chhor dalidar gaayo.
content.meaning: I have received the treasure accumulated over many lifetimes — the world has lost this wealth. No thief can steal it, no moth can destroy it. All poverty has vanished.
content.transliteration:
Janam janam kī pūṅjī pāī,
Jag meṁ sabhī khovāyo.
Khevaṇh nahīṁ koī ṭakkar lāgat,
Chor ḍalidar gāyo.

content.shloka:
Sat ki naav khevatiya Satguru,
Bhav sagar tar aayo.
Meera ke Prabhu Giridhar Nagar,
Harakh harakh jas gaayo.
content.meaning: The boat of Truth with the Satguru as the boatman has carried me across the ocean of worldly existence. Meera's Lord is Giridhar Nagar (Krishna, the lifter of Govardhan) — with joy, she sings His praises.
content.transliteration:
Sat kī nāv khevatiyā Satguru,
Bhav sāgar tar āyo.
Mīrā ke Prabhu Giridhar Nāgar,
Harakh harakh jas gāyo.

content.shloka:
Mere to Giridhar Gopal, doosra na koi,
Jake sir mor mukut, mero pati soi.
Chaadi diye rajya vaibhav, nate kul ki kaani,
Paathaan baithi paachhan, moti main nibhani.
content.meaning: My Lord is Giridhar Gopal, there is no other for me. He who wears the peacock crown upon His head — He alone is my husband. I have renounced royal splendour and the honour of my family. Seated among the saints, I string pearls of devotion.
content.transliteration:
Mere to Giridhara Gopāl, dūsrā na koī,
Jāke sir mor mukuṭ, mero pati soī.
Chāḍi diye rājya vaibhav, nāte kul kī kānī,
Pāṭhāṁ baiṭhī pāchan, motī maiṁ nibhānī.

content.shloka:
Mane chakar rakho ji,
Girdhari laala, mane chakar rakho ji.
Chakar rahungi baag lagaungi,
Nit uthungi darshan paaungi.
content.meaning: Keep me as Your servant, O beloved Giridhari! I shall remain Your servant, tend Your garden, rise early each day, and behold Your divine form.
content.transliteration:
Māne cākar rākho jī,
Girdharī Lāl, māne cākar rākho jī.
Cākar rahūṅgī bāg lagāūṅgī,
Nit uṭhūṅgī darśan pāūṅgī.

content.shloka:
Chalti chaaki dekh ke, diya Kabira roye,
Dui paatan ke beech mein, sabit bacha na koye.
content.meaning: Watching the grinding stones turn, Kabir weeps — between the two millstones of life and death, no one escapes unscathed. Only the one who clings to the axle (the divine Name) is saved.
content.transliteration:
Caltī cākī dekh ke, diyā Kabīrā roye,
Dui pāṭan ke bīc meṁ, sābit bacā na koye.

content.shloka:
Bura jo dekhan main chala, bura na milya koi,
Jo dil khoja aapna, mujh se bura na koi.
content.meaning: When I set out to find evil in the world, I found none. But when I searched my own heart, I found no one worse than myself.
content.transliteration:
Burā jo dekhan maiṁ calā, burā na milyā koī,
Jo dil khojā āpnā, mujh se burā na koī.

content.shloka:
Dukh mein sumiran sab kare, sukh mein kare na koi,
Jo sukh mein sumiran kare, dukh kahe ko hoi.
content.meaning: Everyone remembers God in times of sorrow, but none remember Him in joy. If you remember Him in happiness, why would sorrow ever come?
content.transliteration:
Dukh meṁ sumiran sab kare, sukh meṁ kare na koī,
Jo sukh meṁ sumiran kare, dukh kāhe ko hoī.

content.shloka:
Pothi padh padh jag mua, pandit bhaya na koi,
Dhai akshar prem ka, padhe so pandit hoi.
content.meaning: Reading and reading, the whole world died, yet no one became truly learned. Whoever reads the two-and-a-half letters of love (prem) becomes the real scholar.
content.transliteration:
Pothī paḍh paḍh jag muā, paṇḍit bhayā na koī,
Ḍhāī akṣar prem kā, paḍhe so paṇḍit hoī.

content.shloka:
Kaal kare so aaj kar, aaj kare so ab,
Pal mein pralay hoyegi, bahuri karega kab.
content.meaning: What you plan to do tomorrow, do it today. What you plan for today, do it now. In a moment, destruction may come — when will you do it then?
content.transliteration:
Kāl kare so āj kar, āj kare so ab,
Pal meṁ pralay hoygī, bahuri karegā kab.

content.shloka:
Mala to kar mein phire, jeebh phire mukh maahi,
Manua to chahun dish phire, yeh to sumiran naahi.
content.meaning: The rosary turns in the hand, the tongue moves in the mouth, but the mind wanders in all directions — this is not true remembrance of the Divine.
content.transliteration:
Mālā to kar meṁ phire, jībh phire mukh māhī,
Manuā to cāhuṁ diś phire, yeh to sumiran nāhī.

content.shloka:
Abhanga vani Tukobachi, gajar dare Vitthalachee.
Sadhu santa samaj meli, Pandharpur nagari bhali.
content.meaning: The immortal words of Tukaram resound with the glory of Vitthala. The assembly of saints and holy ones has made the city of Pandharpur truly blessed.
content.transliteration:
Abhaṅga vāṇī Tukobācī, gajar dare Viṭṭhalachī.
Sādhu santa samāj melī, Paṇḍharpur nagarī bhalī.

content.shloka:
Jaga karane Hari, jaag karane Hari,
Anant sukhachya saagara, kadhee dekhaseel hari.
content.meaning: Awake, O Hari! Awake, O Hari! O ocean of infinite bliss, when will I behold You, Lord?
content.transliteration:
Jāg karaṇe Hari, jāg karaṇe Hari,
Anant sukhācyā sāgarā, kadhī dekhśīl Hari.

content.shloka:
Vriksha valli amha soyari vanachare,
Pakshi hi susware aalviti kiti re.
Yethe sakal siddhi bolatichi Vachane,
Yethe Naama smaran kirtanache khune.
content.meaning: Trees and creepers are our kinsfolk, and the forest creatures our friends. The birds sing so sweetly here. Here all spiritual powers speak their wisdom, and the chanting of the Name is the hallmark of kirtan.
content.transliteration:
Vṛkṣa vallī āmhā soyarī vanacāre,
Pakṣī hī susvare ālvitī kitī re.
Yethe sakal siddhī bolatīcī vācane,
Yethe Nāma smaraṇ kīrtanāce khuṇe.

content.shloka:
Tukha mhane aata urasala bhagavant,
Sakalanche de jo aamucha santant.
Je ka ranjale gaanjale, tyasi mhane jo aapule,
Tuka mhane yechi dharma, jano deva Panduranga.
content.meaning: Tuka says, now only God remains. May He give everything to the lineage of saints. Whoever says 'mine' to the afflicted and downtrodden — Tuka says this is true dharma, and that person is Panduranga himself.
content.transliteration:
Tukā mhaṇe ātā urasalā Bhagavant,
Sakalāṅce de jo āmucā santant.
Je kā rāṅjale gāṅjale, tyāsī mhaṇe jo āpule,
Tukā mhaṇe yecī dharmā, jāṇo devā Pāṇḍuraṅgā.

content.shloka:
Sadhu sant yeti ghari, tochi diwali dasara.
Ek tari ovi mhane, Tuka mhanaj jeev re.
content.meaning: When saints and holy ones visit your home, that day itself is Diwali and Dussehra. Say at least one verse of devotion, says Tuka — that is what it means to truly live.
content.transliteration:
Sādhu sant yetī gharī, tocī Divāḷī Dasarā.
Ek tarī ovī mhaṇe, Tukā mhaṇaj jīv re.

content.shloka:
Main nahin maakhan khaayo,
Maiya main nahin maakhan khaayo.
Khilat rahaat moh pe dolat,
Mokhe gher gher mat jaayo.
content.meaning: I have not eaten the butter, O Mother! I have not eaten the butter. Other children keep swinging around me and playing — do not go blaming me in every house.
content.transliteration:
Maiṁ nahīṁ mākhan khāyo,
Maiyā maiṁ nahīṁ mākhan khāyo.
Khilat rahāt moh pe ḍolat,
Mokhe gher gher mat jāyo.

content.shloka:
Graval baat agar moti chai,
Kahat na baat sahi taayo.
Jo main maakhan khayo hai toh,
Daant dikhao bataayo.
content.meaning: The path to Your home is rocky, says the child Krishna. I cannot walk that far. If I really ate the butter, then look — show me my teeth (as proof).
content.transliteration:
Graval bāṭ agar motī cāī,
Kahat na bāt sahī tāyo.
Jo maiṁ mākhan khāyo hai toh,
Dāṁt dikhāo batāyo.

content.shloka:
Sur das ke Prabhu daurhiyo dhaayo,
Nand ke nand kishore.
Mohini moorat shyam sundar,
Brajh mein sabhi kishore.
content.meaning: Surdas's Lord came running quickly — the darling child of Nanda! His enchanting dark-complexioned form is the most beautiful in all of Vraja.
content.transliteration:
Sūrdās ke Prabhu daurhiyo dhāyo,
Nand ke nand Kiśore.
Mohinī mūrat Śyām sundar,
Braj meṁ sabhī Kiśore.

content.shloka:
Akhiyan Hari darshan ki pyasi,
Dekhoon Vrindavan vaasi.
Surdas Prabhu tumhare darshan,
Parasi param sukh rasi.
content.meaning: My eyes thirst for the sight of Lord Hari — I long to see the dweller of Vrindavan. Surdas says, O Lord, beholding You is the supreme treasure of happiness.
content.transliteration:
Akhiyāṁ Hari darśan kī pyāsī,
Dekhūṁ Vṛndāvan vāsī.
Sūrdās Prabhu tumhāre darśan,
Parāsī param sukh rāsī.

content.shloka:
Shri Ramchandra kripalu bhajman,
Haran bhavbhaya daaurnman.
Navkanj lochan kanj mukha, kar kanj pad kanjarunam.
Kandarp aganit amit chhavi, nava neel neeraj sundaram.
content.meaning: Worship Lord Ramchandra, the compassionate one, who destroys the fear and sorrow of worldly existence. His eyes are like fresh lotuses, His face like a lotus, His hands and feet like lotus blossoms. His beauty surpasses millions of Cupids — like a fresh, dark-blue rain cloud, He is magnificent.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Rāmcandra kṛpālu bhajman,
Haraṇ bhavbhay dāruṇman.
Navkañj locan kañj mukhā, kar kañj pad kañjāruṇam.
Kandarp aganit amit chavi, nav nīl nīraj sundaram.

content.shloka:
Pat peet maanahu tadit ruci, shuchi naumi janaka sutaam.
Bhaju deena bandhu dinesha, Daanavdaitya vansha nikandanam.
Raghunand anand kand, Kaushal chand Dasharath nandanam.
content.meaning: Her yellow garments shine like lightning — I bow to the pure daughter of Janaka. Worship the friend of the poor, Lord of the humble, destroyer of the demon races. He is Raghunanda, the root of all bliss, the moon of Kaushalya, the darling son of Dasharatha.
content.transliteration:
Paṭ pīt mānahu taḍit rucī, śucī naumī Janak sutām.
Bhaju dīna bandhu dīneśa, Dānavdaitya vaṁś nikandanam.
Raghunand ānand kand, Kauśal cand Daśarath nandanam.

content.shloka:
Sir mukut kundale tilak charu udaar ang garha chandam.
Manihaar padak undee mala, tanu sajat sar sundaram.
Shiv virinji sureshi sevahi, Tulsi hit janman.
content.meaning: His head adorned with a crown, earrings, a beautiful tilak, His magnificent body decorated with sandalwood paste. Jewelled necklaces, pendants, and garlands adorn His beautiful form. Shiva, Brahma, and Indra serve Him — Tulsi says, it is for our benefit that He took birth.
content.transliteration:
Sir mukuṭ kuṇḍale tilak cāru udār aṅg garhā candanam.
Manihār padak undī mālā, tanu sājat sar sundaram.
Śiv Virīñci Sureśī sevahī, Tulasī hit janmān.

content.shloka:
Ram se badhkar Ram ka naam,
Ram se badhkar Ram ka naam.
Tulsi sada Hari cheraa,
Karke vichar yeh kaam.
content.meaning: Greater than Rama Himself is Rama's name! Greater than Rama Himself is Rama's name. Tulsi is forever the servant of Lord Hari — having reflected deeply, this is the conclusion.
content.transliteration:
Rām se baḍhkar Rām kā nām,
Rām se baḍhkar Rām kā nām.
Tulasī sadā Hari cerā,
Karke vicār yeh kām.

content.shloka:
Naache Vitthala naache Vithoo,
Naamyachi gadi Vitthoo naache.
Dev suthaar kambar keli, Namdev aang paridhaan kayli.
content.meaning: Vitthala dances, Vitthoo dances! On Namdev's singing, Vitthala dances. The Lord, like a carpenter, made the body — and Namdev clothed that body with devotion.
content.transliteration:
Nāce Viṭṭhala nāce Viṭhū,
Nāmyācī gaḍī Viṭhū nāce.
Dev suthār kambar kelī, Nāmdev āṅg paridhān kaylī.

content.shloka:
Aadhi Rachila Vithoo maga rachili veet,
Devala bandha kalee Nama tyavar cheet.
Naache Vitthala, Naache Vithoo.
content.meaning: First Vitthala was created, then the brick was made. The temple was built, and Namdev's mind is fixed upon Him. Vitthala dances, Vitthoo dances!
content.transliteration:
Ādhī Racilā Viṭhū mag racilī vīṭ,
Devāla bandhā kelī Nāmā tyāvar cīt.
Nāce Viṭṭhala, Nāce Viṭhū.

content.shloka:
Naama mhane maza Vitthala bhala,
Tyachiye payi maza jeev ovalaala.
Hari maza mukha, Hari maza doola,
Hari sarvabhaava naamache ghola.
content.meaning: Namdev says, my Vitthala is wonderful! My life is a sacrifice at His feet. Hari is my face, Hari is my beloved — Hari pervades everything, and Nama's heart is absorbed in Him.
content.transliteration:
Nāmā mhaṇe māzā Viṭṭhala bhalā,
Tyāciye pāyī māzā jīv ovaḷālā.
Hari māzā mukhā, Hari māzā dūlā,
Hari sarvabhāvā Nāmāce gholā.

content.shloka:
Zhaale mohre naama yache, deva Vitthal kaise ugavale,
Nirmal manase pujile, Naama Haripath ghetale.
content.meaning: The seed of the Name was sown, and Lord Vitthala sprouted forth. With a pure mind He was worshipped — Namdev took the path of Hari.
content.transliteration:
Jhāle mohre nāmā yāce, devā Viṭṭhal kaise ugavale,
Nirmal mānase pūjile, Nāmā Haripāth ghetale.

content.shloka:
Eka tari Vitthala mhana re baa,
Yene honti sarvahi kaama.
Pandhariche bhoot maher, tya naama gheta sukh maher.
content.meaning: Say 'Vitthala' at least once, O friend! By this all your works will be accomplished. The spirit of Pandharpur is like a mother's home — taking that Name gives the comfort of a mother's embrace.
content.transliteration:
Ekā tarī Viṭṭhala mhaṇā re bā,
Yeṇe hontī sarvahī kāmā.
Paṇḍharīce bhūt māher, tyā nāmā ghetā sukh māher.

content.shloka:
Dev maza vithu savala, saguna nirgun aakala.
Rukmini vallabh maher, Eknath tyacha putra.
content.meaning: My God is the dark-complexioned Vitthu — He is both with form and formless, beyond comprehension. He is the beloved of Rukmini — Eknath is His child.
content.transliteration:
Dev māzā Viṭhū sāvḷā, saguṇ nirguṇ ākḷā.
Rukmiṇī vallabh māher, Eknāth tyācā putrā.

content.shloka:
Kanha re doot kanha re doot,
Sangati dhara Vitthal soot.
Sant sangati parama pavitra,
Eknathi bhajan amrut charitra.
content.meaning: Where are the messengers, where are the messengers? Hold the thread of Vitthala's company. The company of saints is supremely purifying — Eknath's bhajans are the nectar of divine life.
content.transliteration:
Kānhā re dūt kānhā re dūt,
Saṅgatī dharā Viṭṭhal sūt.
Sant saṅgatī paramā pavitrā,
Eknāthī bhajan amṛt caritrā.

content.shloka:
Devachi krupahi je ghadali aapana,
Sant sanga ladhale he bhagya sampurn.
Eka Janardani sanga dharile, dev Vitthal labh kele.
content.meaning: By God's grace this has come to pass — the fortune of finding saintly company is complete. With one-pointed devotion to Lord Janardana, the treasure of Lord Vitthala is obtained.
content.transliteration:
Devācī kṛpāhī je ghaḍalī āpaṇā,
Sant saṅga lādhale he bhāgya sampūrṇ.
Ekā Janārdanī saṅga dharile, dev Viṭṭhal lābh kele.

content.shloka:
Gana gana gana gana Ganadheeshaa,
Sarva siddhi dayaka deva Ganeshaa.
Dhaav paav maza Gajaananaa,
Laav laav Shri Hari chi karunaa.
content.meaning: Sing, sing, sing of the Lord of the Ganas (Ganesha)! The deity who bestows all accomplishments. Rush to my aid, O Gajanana! Shower upon me the compassion of Lord Hari.
content.transliteration:
Gaṇa gaṇa gaṇa gaṇa Gaṇādhīśā,
Sarva siddhi dāyakā devā Gaṇeśā.
Dhāv pāv māzā Gajānanā,
Lāv lāv Śrī Hari cī karuṇā.

content.shloka:
Mana sajjana bhakti panthe chalaa,
Paramartha karani thaav re,
Vichar karuniya mukhya karaa,
Anubhav ghya re sakala.
content.meaning: O good mind, walk the path of devotion! Make your abode in spiritual practice. Reflect deeply and choose what is essential — experience it all fully.
content.transliteration:
Manā sajjanā bhakti panthe calā,
Paramārtha karaṇī ṭhāv re,
Vicār karuṇiyā mukhya karā,
Anubhav ghyā re sakal.

content.shloka:
Jaya jaya Raghuveer samartha,
Sada karoni tujha karunaa artha.
Karoni naam ghosh uttama,
Tuka mhane Rama param.
content.meaning: Victory, victory to the mighty Raghuveer (Rama)! We always seek Your compassion and grace. Chanting Your glorious Name is the highest practice — Tuka says, Rama is the Supreme.
content.transliteration:
Jayā jayā Raghuvīr samarthā,
Sadā karonī tujhā karuṇā arthā.
Karonī nām ghoṣ uttamā,
Tukā mhaṇe Rāmā param.

content.shloka:
Mana he saambhal aata re vichaari,
Tuza tujha paashi aahe re.
Prapaanch karuni Hari bajan keli,
Daas Ramdas mhane saukhya ailii.
content.meaning: O mind, listen now and reflect carefully — your own true self is with you always. By living in the world while chanting Hari's name, Servant Ramdas says happiness arrives.
content.transliteration:
Manā he sāmbhaḷ ātā re vicārī,
Tuzā tujhā pāśī āhe re.
Prapañc karunī Hari bhajan kelī,
Dās Rāmdās mhaṇe saukhya āilī.

content.shloka:
Manache shloka mhanaa re mhanaa,
Vichar karuniya nijadhaam jaanaa.
Samarth Ramdas swaami sanga,
Ghya re bhetavi Panduranga.
content.meaning: Recite the verses addressed to the mind, recite them! Reflect deeply and journey to your true abode. With the company of Lord Samarth Ramdas Swami, you shall attain the vision of Panduranga.
content.transliteration:
Mānāce śloka mhaṇā re mhaṇā,
Vicār karuṇiyā nijdhām jāṇā.
Samarth Rāmdās Svāmī saṅgā,
Ghyā re bheṭavī Pāṇḍuraṅgā.
